options: Variable-size — it stays open while events keep arriving close together, and closes after a timeout of inactivity
Fixed-size and non-overlapping, like a tumbling window
Fixed-size but overlapping, like a hopping window
A window that never closes
questions.explain: Unlike tumbling or hopping, a session window has no fixed clock at all — a gap of inactivity decides the boundary.

questions.q: Why doesn't a fixed 5-minute tumbling window draw a good boundary around a rider's single burst of app activity?
options: The activity might last 90 seconds or 40 minutes depending on the rider, and a fixed window can't adapt to that variability
Tumbling windows can't process app activity data at all
Tumbling windows always produce more accurate results than session windows
There's no real difference — a tumbling window works fine here
questions.explain: A session window watches for a gap of inactivity instead, closing wherever that gap actually falls.

questions.q: What setting controls when a session window closes?
options: A timeout — the gap of inactivity that must pass with nothing new arriving
A fixed window size in minutes
A hop size
The number of events received
questions.explain: The session stays open as long as events keep arriving within the timeout, and closes once that gap passes.

questions.q: Why are session windows usually grouped by a key like RiderId?
options: So each rider gets their own independently-timed sessions, rather than one global session across every rider at once
Grouping is required by KQL syntax and has no conceptual purpose
To make the window fixed-size instead of variable
RiderId is required for tumbling windows, not session windows
questions.explain: Without grouping, one rider's inactivity gap would incorrectly affect every other rider's session.

questions.q: Which Eventstream canvas Window transformation setting configures a session window's boundary?
options: Timeout, set to a duration of inactivity
Hop size
Window size, set to a fixed duration
Watermark delay
questions.explain: Session is configured with a timeout instead of a fixed size, unlike Tumbling or Sliding.
